blocks.eyebrow: Why last time did not hold
blocks.heading: You were doing it right. You were using something that only reaches the top layer.
quotes: “Two months of daily use. It lightened a little, then stopped there.”
“The jar runs out and the pigment comes back, sometimes darker than before.”
“The ingredient list is all vague groupings. No idea how much of anything is in there.”
“What worries me most is using something with corticosteroids without knowing.”

explainer.heading: Brightening the epidermis does not reach where the pigment is made
body: Melanin is produced by cells sitting deeper down. A product acting only on the surface shows results in the first few weeks, then stops — because underneath, everything continues as before.

This jar's formula aims at three things at once: limiting the signal to produce pigment, supporting the turnover of already-darkened cells, and reinforcing the barrier so darkening is less likely to return.
In exchange, you need patience measured in weeks rather than days. And you need sun protection. Skip sunscreen and no product holds its result — that is a precondition, not advice.

blocks.eyebrow: Compare the photos with your own skin
blocks.heading: Which kinds of melasma this jar suits — and when it doesn’t
blocks.intro: We are a reseller. Selling the wrong thing to the wrong person means you use it for a few weeks and give up — a loss on both sides. So the cases this jar is not for, we tell you up front.

items.label: Patchy melasma, a few years old
items.aka: epidermal melasma — pigment near the surface

image.alt: Close-up of a light-brown melasma patch with defined edges on the cheek

items.body: Brown patches with clear edges, the pigment still near the surface. This is the group the cream alone suits best: the sealing step keeps the actives on your skin overnight. You still need sunscreen every morning.

items.label: Deep or mixed melasma
items.aka: pigment sits deeper, edges look blurred

image.alt: Close-up of deep melasma: a darker area with blurred edges on the cheek

items.body: The cream still works, but on its own the deeper-absorbing step is missing, so progress is noticeably slower. Worth adding the serum — which is exactly what the combo is for.
items.fitNote: Usable — but look at the combo

items.label: Melasma that appeared in or after pregnancy

image.alt: Close-up of melasma on the cheek, the kind often linked to hormonal change

items.body: If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, ask your doctor before using it — that advice is printed on the pack. After that, choose between the cream alone and the combo by how deep the pigment sits, as above.
items.fitNote: Pregnant or nursing: ask your doctor first

items.label: Marks left after breakouts

image.alt: Close-up of skin with several brown marks left after acne

items.body: The NIO-NAG in this jar is aimed at post-inflammatory pigment, but the cream goes on the whole face. If what you have is mostly individual post-acne marks, Mocha’s spot gel for dark marks is the better tool.
items.fitNote: The spot gel is a better fit

items.label: Irritated, flaking or freshly peeled skin
items.body: Let your skin settle first. Adding actives to a damaged barrier is the surest way to make it react harder. If irritation starts while you are using it, stop.

items.label: A dark patch that spreads or changes fast
items.body: A dark area that grows quickly, changes colour or shape, is raised, itches or bleeds is not a job for a jar of cream. See a dermatologist first — we won’t sell you that hope.

blocks.caption: Close-ups illustrating each skin condition (the brand's own image library) — not before-and-after photos of the product. Not sure whether your pigment is shallow or deep? Send us a photo on Zalo and an adviser will take a look before you order.

blocks.heading: Shallow or deep melasma decides whether you need one step or two
blocks.intro: The cream works on the surface of your skin overnight. The deeper the pigment, the more it pays to add a step that gets actives in before the cream.

items.label: The night cream layer
items.body: The last step at night: it seals in moisture and keeps the actives on your skin until morning. By day, what sits on the surface should be sunscreen.

items.label: Patchy melasma
items.body: Pigment sits near the surface, in the epidermis, with clear edges. This is where the cream on its own fits most naturally.

items.label: Deep melasma
items.body: Pigment reaches down into the dermis and the edges blur. The cream alone is much slower here; add the serum before it to cover both steps.

items.label: Mixed melasma
items.body: Part shallow, part deep — so plan for it as you would for deep melasma: the two-step combo suits it better than the cream alone.

blocks.footnote: Illustrative diagram, not to scale. You can’t always tell shallow pigment from deep by eye — if you’re unsure, send a photo to an adviser before you choose.

blocks.heading: The cream alone, or both steps?
blocks.intro: Worth answering before you order, not after the first jar runs out. The table below states the difference plainly.

rows.name: Tranexamic Acid 3%
rows.role: Among the more widely studied topical options for softening areas darkened by excess pigment.

rows.name: NIO-NAG 2%
rows.role: A glucosamine derivative that helps regulate pigment formation.

rows.name: Ceramide 1%
rows.role: A structural part of the skin barrier that helps hold moisture.

rows.name: Bakuchiol 2%
rows.role: A plant-derived alternative to retinol studied for easily irritated skin; it does not increase light sensitivity.
rows.suitedFor: Sensitive skin, skin that does not tolerate retinol

rows.name: Vietnam Bio-white Complex 3%
rows.role: The same native complex as the serum, in a cream that stays on skin longer.

rows.name: Black Truffle Extract 2%
rows.role: Black truffle extract, in a cream that stays on the skin overnight.

blocks.eyebrow: Where it sits in the day
blocks.heading: This jar is the last step at night
blocks.intro: No need to change the routine you have. Just put it in the right place — and keep the morning sunscreen.

steps.label: Moisturise
steps.note: Whatever you already use; no need to change it.

steps.label: Sunscreen
steps.note: Skip this and pigment returns whatever you applied the night before.

steps.label: Remove make-up and cleanse
steps.note: Actives land on residue if any is left on the skin.

steps.label: Pat completely dry
steps.note: Damp skin dilutes the cream and reduces how much goes in.

steps.label: Smart Brightening X3 cream
steps.note: A fingertip's worth, dotted at five points and spread. Massage darker areas for one to two minutes.

blocks.footnote: Use it every other night for the first week so your skin adjusts, then nightly. Patch test on the neck and watch for 30–45 minutes before the first full use.

blocks.heading: Three steps, once or twice a day
blocks.intro: The order below is taken from the instructions supplied with the product.

items.heading: Cleanse
items.body: Wash and dry your face first. Damp skin or leftover make-up both reduce how much is absorbed.

items.heading: Take the right amount
items.body: About the size of one fingertip joint, dotted evenly on five points: forehead, both cheeks, nose and chin.

items.heading: Apply and massage
items.body: Spread outwards and upwards over face and neck, avoiding the eye area. Massage darker patches for one to two minutes.

blocks.footnote: Patch-test on the neck and watch for 30–45 minutes before using it on the whole face. Sunscreen in the morning is not optional — without it pigmentation returns whatever product you use.

items.q: Is the cream enough on its own?
items.a: The cream is the step that seals moisture in and keeps the actives on the skin. If you also want a deeper-penetrating step you need the serum — that is what the combo is for. Plainly: the cream on its own is a valid routine, just a slower one than using both steps.
The formula uses Bakuchiol instead of retinol and contains no corticosteroids or hydroquinone. Still patch-test on the neck and watch for 30–45 minutes before using it on the whole face.
The product contains no retinoids. Even so, if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, ask a doctor before using any skincare product.
Keep away from heat and direct sunlight, close the lid after use, keep out of reach of children. Avoid contact with the eyes; if it gets in, rinse immediately with clean water.
